analysis:
The PR changes only CHANGELOG.md (documentation). It renames the v0.10.8 candidate section to v0.10.9, adds many release notes, and marks v0.10.8 as published. No executable code, policy or configuration is modified, so no direct security regression is introduced.

I read the notes that describe security-relevant behavior and found none that contradict the canonical threat model:
- Pair and cluster rollout, leftover single-Mac serving, version-split detection and the TB-012 add-on hold. These touch A-018 and T-059/T-060, but they are only descriptions of changes made elsewhere.
- `darkbloom cluster gpu-limit`, a root boot job behind an owner confirmation and an administrator prompt. This matches TB-014, A-020 and T-062, and the notes say Darkbloom never changes the limit on its own.
- The sandbox `--disk` option and the installer, which TB-013 and T-061 cover.
- CI changes, including the watchdog token being limited to cancel and re-run of this repository's workflow runs and writing a check run, the Xcode 27.2 toolchain, and the Date-comparison weak-import check, which matches the canonical header note.
- Registration, described as unchanged ('darkbloom_cluster_runtime_v2' block, same fields). I could not verify this against code; it is a claim made in the changelog only.

One documented known limitation is that DevNet can read production pair state and `darkbloom-dev cluster pair --forget` can remove production's login job when both apps are installed. This is disclosed, not a new regression. The threat model may need a later update if it is not already covered by a retained entry, which I could not check without code.

The changelog makes claims about code behavior that I cannot verify from this diff alone: the pair approval cap and registration unchanged, and the single-Mac step-aside logic. The corresponding source commits need their own review. Nothing here is a concrete vulnerability.
